title: Astrid and the Orchard
premise: In 1793, Dominic Delacroix, a young woman disguised as a mapmaker's apprentice, is completing the atlas her dying master spent his life on when revolutionary soldiers requisition the town of Vireloup and seize the master's ledger—the only record of every family's true names and loyalties. As the army prepares to deport 'suspect' households, Dominic discovers the ledger contains a hidden page naming her own forged identity, and that a berth on the last evacuation barge can be bought with information. To save the found family she never admitted was hers, she must trade the atlas itself, betraying her dead master's life's work to the men who killed him—choosing living loyalty over dead truth.
about_author: J. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing provincial maps and municipal ledgers in the French countryside. Their fiction grew out of the marginalia—names, debts, and small rebellions—found in the records of people history forgot.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She inks the final coastline of Master Aubertin's atlas, hiding her own name from its dedication, and reflects on how maps keep history at arm's length. Emotional beat: quiet grief and deliberate invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Remembers
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She catalogs the town ledger—every household, debt, and secret—for the estate sale, noting which neighbors were kind to a friendless apprentice. Beat: reluctant tenderness toward Vireloup.

chapters.title: Boots on the Bridge
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Revolutionary soldiers requisition the town at dawn; Captain Roche demands all civic records, including the ledger. She hides one loose page inside the atlas frame. Beat: first crack in her belief that history happens elsewhere.

chapters.title: The Berth List
chapters.summary: Roche's POV. He drafts evacuation lists for the suspect families, weighing orders against conscience, and notices an apprentice who watches too carefully. Beat: cold arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: Names Are Not Neutral
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The Marceau family, who fed her through two hard winters, is marked for deportation; their daughter Sylvie begs Dominic to use her access to the records room. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Forgery of One's Own
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Flashback chapter: how Aubertin took in a runaway girl, taught her cartography, and helped forge her papers as his nephew. Beat: the found family she has been denying.

chapters.title: The Price of Ink
chapters.summary: Sylvie's POV. Sylvie trades her mother's silver for a false transit pass and discovers someone else already altered the berth list—in Dominic's handwriting. Beat: betrayal and confusion.

chapters.title: Roche's Map Room
chapters.summary: Roche's POV. Interrogating the archive, he finds the hidden page: a list of informants, including Aubertin's killer, Sergeant Vaillant. He begins to doubt whose side the paperwork serves. Beat: dawning complicity.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Borders
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She confronts Vaillant about Aubertin's death; he reveals the master died protecting the informant page—and that it names Dominic's real birth family. Beat: identity shaken.

chapters.title: The Atlas as Hostage
chapters.summary: Roche's POV. Command orders the atlas confiscated as strategic material; Roche delays, using it to bargain for softer treatment of the townsfolk. Beat: a bureaucrat growing a spine.

chapters.title: Three Names, One Berth
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The final barge has one berth left beyond the Marceaus' allocation: enough for Sylvie or for old Père Fournier, who once sheltered her. She must choose. Beat: the central dilemma made flesh.

chapters.title: What Sylvie Would Do
chapters.summary: Sylvie's POV. Sylvie learns of the choice and secretly withdraws herself, forging Dominic's signature to give the berth to Fournier. Beat: love expressed as deception.

chapters.title: Night Cartography
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Mapping the river by moonlight, she finds a disused lock that could take a second boat past the checkpoint—if someone stays behind to work it manually. Beat: hope with a terrible price tag.

chapters.title: Vaillant's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vaillant's POV. Vaillant blackmails Roche with the informant page, demanding the atlas be burned and the Marceaus deported as leverage. Beat: villainy revealed as fear.

chapters.title: The Burning of Marginalia
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Soldiers burn 'subversive documents'; Dominic rescues the ledger's loose pages at risk of exposure, and Roche looks away deliberately. Beat: an enemy becomes an uncertain ally.

chapters.title: Confession at the Lock
chapters.summary: Dominic and Sylvie, dual focus. On the riverbank, each confesses her forgery; anger gives way to the recognition that they have both been protecting each other badly. Beat: truth as the price of real family.

chapters.title: The Last Manifest
chapters.summary: Roche's POV. Roche alters the manifest himself, adding names and erasing others, knowing it will end his career—or his life. Beat: sacrifice by pen stroke.

chapters.title: Vaillant Comes for the Atlas
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Vaillant catches her copying the atlas's key plates for escape routes; a standoff in the map room where she offers him the informant page in exchange for the barge's safe passage. Beat: climax of wits.

chapters.title: Water Rising
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The evacuation night: the lock groans open, Fournier works the mechanism as the soldiers close in, and the second boat slips through. Beat: terror and grace under pressure.

chapters.title: The Cost of the Crossing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Fournier is taken; Vaillant reports the escape but Roche buries the evidence, and the Marceaus reach free water. Dominic holds the rescued pages—her family's names intact. Beat: grief braided with victory.

chapters.title: A New Projection
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In exile with the Marceaus, she begins drawing a new map—not of territory but of the route that saved them, signing it with her true name for the first time. Beat: belonging claimed openly.

chapters.title: The Orchard in Spring
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, years later. She returns to Vireloup under amnesty, plants a tree over Fournier's unmarked grave, and donates the completed atlas to the town—with the ledger's names restored beside it. Beat: reconciliation of loyalty and truth; home redefined.
